title: SinkCast: An Empirical Study of Inference-Time Correction for BF16 RoPE Shift-Invariance

contributions.purpose: Restore BF16 RoPE shift-invariance at low overhead by correcting only attention-sink positions.
contributions.mechanism: SinkCast: run BF16 FlashAttention to get output and log-sum-exp statistics, selectively recompute sink-key logits in FP32, then apply a closed-form correction (subtract BF16 sink contribution, rescale, add FP32-corrected sink contribution) to the output.
contributions.evaluation: Presented as a three-stage method on Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B-v0.3 with FlashAttention-2; gap closure at most 23.6% (Llama, K=4) and 36.3% (Mistral, K=1), far below the 80% target.
contributions.domain: LLM inference / attention numerical precision (BF16 RoPE, position-independent KV caching)
contributions.source_quote: We propose SinkCast, a principled inference-time correction method that selectively recomputes sink-key attention logits in FP32 and applies closed-form corrections to BF16 FlashAttention outputs.

contributions.purpose: Test whether BF16 shift-error is localized at attention sinks, the premise underlying SinkCast.
contributions.mechanism: Measure the D_logit shift-error metric across key indices (j in {0,1,2,8,64}) under position offsets 0 vs 4096 and compute the sink key's fraction of total error.
contributions.evaluation: The sink key (j=0) has the lowest D_logit, accounting for only 5.0% (Llama) and 8.5% (Mistral) of total shift-error, far below the 50% threshold; localization premise refuted.
contributions.source_quote: We provide comprehensive evaluation demonstrating that the attention sink localization hypothesis does not hold: the sink key contributes only 5-8% of total BF16 shift-error.

contributions.purpose: Explain why sink-focused correction fails and guide future approaches.
contributions.mechanism: Analyze that BF16 rotation precision loss affects all key positions proportionally to rotation angle rather than concentrating at sinks; downstream evaluation on RULER and LongBench under position shift.
contributions.evaluation: Overall downstream improvement is -0.91 points (SinkCast worse than BF16 baseline); increasing corrected keys K beyond optimum degrades further (Llama K=16 gives -19.6% gap closure).
contributions.source_quote: We analyze why sink-focused correction fails, showing that BF16 rotation precision loss affects all key positions equally, and discuss implications for future approaches to this problem.

self_declared_provenance.quote: We hypothesize that BF16 shift-error concentrates at attention sink positions-the initial tokens that receive disproportionate attention regardless of semantic relevance (Xiao et al., 2023). If true, selectively correcting only sink-key attention logits could restore shift-invariance with minimal computational overhead.
The concentration of attention at sink positions motivated our hypothesis that correcting sink-key errors might address a substantial portion of BF16 shift-error.
Wang et al. (2024) demonstrated that BF16 RoPE computation violates shift-invariance, causing performance degradation in long-context training.
These systems rely on RoPE's shift-invariance property ... BF16 precision violations of this property introduce errors when reusing caches at shifted positions.

notes: Explicit negative-result paper: sink localization premise refuted (sink key only 5-8% of error), gap closure 23-36% vs 80% target, and downstream improvement -0.91 points (no benefit); title/abstract frame it as negative results.
